source: MTA Bus Stop Ridership Estimates (data.ny.gov fvdm-uavx), boardings estimated from Automatic Passenger Counters on board MTA buses. In October 2026 the MTA replaced raw counter boardings in this dataset with these estimates for every month from January 2024; all months here use the new method.
tapsSource: MTA Bus Hourly Ridership (data.ny.gov kv7t-n8in for months through 2024, gxb3-akrn from January 2025), OMNY and MetroCard entries by route.

definitions.total: Estimated boardings on the route that month, every day of the week.
definitions.wdAvg: Monday-Friday boardings that month divided by the number of calendar weekdays in the month. Public holidays are counted as weekdays, so months containing them read slightly low.
definitions.months: Only calendar months with data for all seven days of the week are included.
definitions.caveat: These are MTA estimates built from passenger counters, which not every bus carries; the MTA scales them up to stand for all riders. Before October 2026 the dataset held unscaled counter boardings, which ran far lower, so figures saved from earlier versions of this file are not comparable.
definitions.tapsTotal: Fare taps: every OMNY tap and MetroCard swipe that let a rider onto a bus on the route that month, including free transfers from another bus or the subway. It is a count of paid entries, not of riders: people who board without paying are not in it, and the MTA estimates that a very large share of bus riders do not pay (about 45 to 50 percent on local buses in 2024-2026, MTA Bus Fare Evasion dataset, data.ny.gov uv5h-dfhp). Null where the fare dataset does not cover every day of the month (a day with almost no taps, such as Jan 10-15, 2026, counts as missing), or where the route has no rows in it that month.
definitions.tapsWdAvg: Monday-Friday fare taps that month divided by the number of calendar weekdays in the month, the same denominator as wdAvg.
definitions.ratio: Estimated boardings per fare tap: wdAvg divided by tapsWdAvg, rounded to three decimals. Null where either is missing or zero. A ratio of 1.5 means the MTA estimates three boardings for every two paid entries. It is not an evasion rate: taps include free transfers, and both series are estimates with their own gaps. Still, because the boardings now stand for all riders, a ratio well above 1 is broadly consistent with the MTA fare evasion estimate (about half of local riders not paying implies a ratio near 2 on local routes). If buses go fare-free, taps stop and the estimates are the only measure left; this series records how the two lined up, route by route, beforehand.
definitions.system.tapsTotal: Every fare tap in the dataset that month, all routes, including any that have no counter data (see tapsUnmatched).
definitions.estimatesJoint: Since October 2026 the MTA also reports ridership estimates for the Q52 SBS and Q53 SBS together, as Q52/53+. Both routes carry the pair's combined total and wdAvg; they are counted once in the system figures.
definitions.tapsJoint: The MTA notes that fare data for the Q52 SBS and Q53 SBS are reported together, so the split between them is not reliable. Both routes carry the COMBINED taps of the pair, and their ratio is the pair's combined counters over the pair's combined taps. Do not add the two routes' taps together.
definitions.routeIds: Route keys use the spelling of the live MTA feed and GTFS (for example Q06, not Q6). Counter and fare-tap ids are matched after uppercasing and dropping leading zeros after the letter prefix; routeIdChanges lists every counter id that was rewritten.
definitions.breaks: Dates when a route's ridership stops being comparable with its own history because the route itself changed. The Queens bus network redesign took effect in two phases in 2025: routes were renumbered, rerouted, merged and created, so a Queens route before its change date is not the same route afterward. Each route's exact date is in routeDates; breakMonths on a route lists the month(s) containing its change date. Checked and not inside this series: the Bronx local bus network redesign, implemented June 2022, and the Brooklyn redesign, still in planning (mta.info/project/brooklyn-bus-network-redesign, updated Sep 11, 2026).

breaks.label: Queens bus network redesign, phase 1
breaks.quote: The first phase, with nearly two thirds of the changes, launched on June 29.
breaks.routes_quote: Most routes will change on either June 29 or August 31. Routes without Sunday service will change on either June 30 or September 2.

breaks.label: Queens bus network redesign, phase 2
breaks.quote: The second and last phase began Sunday, Aug. 31, and today marks the full implementation of the redesign.
breaks.routes_quote: Most routes will change on either June 29 or August 31. Routes without Sunday service will change on either June 30 or September 2.
